response.text:
I can’t view or inspect images in this session, so I have not seen the attached warehouse photo and I cannot verify what it shows or read the safety sign. I won’t guess the sign text or describe the scene as if I examined it.

What I can do right now
- Explain common kinds of warehouse safety signs and the typical wording and meanings (see examples below).
- Advise how to capture or extract the sign text (photo and OCR tips).
- Interpret or rewrite the sign (safety guidance, compliance language, translations, suggested corrective actions) if you paste the sign text or a clear transcription here.
- Tell you how to re-send the image or use an OCR tool so I can help with the exact wording.

Common types of warehouse safety signs and typical text (examples only)
- Warning (yellow/black): “Caution: Forklifts Operating”, “Watch for Forklifts”, “Caution: Wet Floor”
- Mandatory (blue/white): “Hard Hats Required Beyond This Point”, “Protective Eyewear Must Be Worn”
- Prohibition (red/white): “No Smoking”, “No Unauthorized Entry”
- Emergency/Exit (green/white): “Emergency Exit”, “First Aid Kit”
- Regulatory / Site-specific: “Authorized Personnel Only”, “Lockout/Tagout Procedures Enforced”, “High Voltage / Keep Out”
These are examples — not a statement about your image.

How to get an accurate read of the sign
- If possible, crop the photo to the sign and make a straight-on close-up to avoid perspective distortion.
- Improve contrast: take the photo in good light, remove glare, or increase contrast in an image editor.
- Use an OCR app or tool (examples: Google Lens, Microsoft OneNote/Office Lens, Adobe Scan, or online OCR services) to extract the printed text, then paste the result here.
- If the sign is small or blurred, try retaking the picture from closer or with a higher-resolution camera.

If you want me to help now
- Paste the exact text of the sign (or type what you can make out), and I’ll interpret it, suggest any safety actions or reword it for clarity/compliance, or translate it.
- Or re-upload the image in a session with image-inspection enabled, or tell me which OCR tool you used and paste its output.

Which would you prefer?
